_note: The stand-in opponent of M3 (spec 21): a simple, legal player so matches can be played and the rules fuzzed. 'values' is what it loads; 'docs' gives each value's unit, source and note. M4's opponent replaces it and this file.

aim_error_rad.note: Standard deviation of the error added to the aim it chose. 0.004 rad is 4 mm at a metre: it pots straight balls and misses long cuts.

speed_error.note: Standard deviation of its cue speed as a fraction of the speed it chose. The speed stays between 0.3 m/s and the physics' maximum.

max_cut_rad.note: It does not try a pot with a wider cut than this (60 degrees).

pot_speed_m_s.note: Cue speed for a pot with a metre of travel in all, cue ball and object ball together. It goes with the square root of the travel and up with the cut, inside the physics' limits, and is halved, up to twice, when the simulated cue ball follows the pot in.

safety_speed_m_s.note: Cue speed when it has no pot and plays to hit a ball on and leave it, and for its escapes from a snooker.

max_sims.source: ours; spec 10.6 allows the real opponent 1.5 s. Measured on the development PC over 1,000 frames of ofs_sim_cli match: 0.17 ms a stroke on average, 2.1 ms at worst
max_sims.note: How many candidate strokes it may simulate on the whole table before choosing, so one decision stays a few milliseconds on the phone. 0 plays its first choice unchecked. Aiming an escape off the cushions also simulates the cue ball alone, at most 40 times (kCourses in standin.cpp), each a small share of one of these.

concede_required_points.source: Section 4 Rule 2(b): a player may concede only when penalty points are required; the threshold is ours
concede_required_points.note: It concedes when it needs at least this many penalty points and no red is left on the table.
